hero.title: 🎵 Song Title Generator

article.intro: A song title is a hook before anyone has heard a note. This **song title generator** gives you titles in the shapes songwriters use most: a single striking word, an action with a story in it ("Chasing Satellites"), or a place ("Rooftop Lullaby"). Use one as a title, or as a prompt to write from.

sections.heading: Titles that stick
sections.content:
• Use the hook. Most memorable titles are the line people sing back: if the chorus repeats a phrase, that's often your title.
  • One word can carry a song if it's vivid: Static, Undertow, Wildfire.
  • A small story beats a big idea. "Waiting for the Last Train" says more than "Loneliness".
  • Search it. Titles aren't protected, but a title shared by a huge hit will bury yours in search results.

sections.heading: Using a title as a prompt
sections.content:
Songwriters often start from a title and write towards it. Generate a few, pick the one that makes you ask a question (who is chasing satellites, and why?), and answer it in the verses.

For the record they'll end up on, try the Album Name Generator; for the band, the Band Name Generator.

For a title that sounds like a particular genre, the music genre name generators have album formats built from how each genre writes its titles, from emo to country.

faqs.question: Can song titles be copyrighted?
faqs.answer: Generally no: titles are too short to be protected by copyright, which is why many songs share a title. A famous title may still bury yours in search results, so check first. This isn't legal advice.

faqs.question: Should the title be in the lyrics?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. Listeners remember songs by the words they sing, so a title that matches the hook is easier to find.
